prompt: The pentagon below has three right angles. Find its area.

solutions.title: Rectangle minus a triangle
solutions.body:
The pentagon is a $10\times10$ square with the top-right corner cut off. The cut-off right triangle has horizontal leg $10 - 4 = 6$ and vertical leg $10 - 2 = 8$ (and hypotenuse $10$ ✓, a $6$-$8$-$10$ triangle).

Area $= 100 - \frac12\cdot6\cdot8 = 100 - 24 = 76$.

**Answer: 76**

solutions.title: Split into pieces
solutions.body:
Cut vertically at $x = 4$: a $4\times10$ rectangle (area $40$), plus a trapezoid of width $6$ with parallel vertical sides $10$ and $2$: area $\frac{10+2}{2}\cdot6 = 36$. Total $76$.

**Answer: 76**

prompt: Let $p_1 = 2$, $p_2 = 3$, $p_3 = 5$, $\ldots$ be the sequence of prime numbers. Find the least positive even integer $n$ so that $p_1 + p_2 + p_3 + \cdots + p_n$ is not prime.

solutions.title: Why only even n are interesting
solutions.body:
For even $n$ the sum is $2$ plus an odd number of odd primes, so it is odd and has a chance to be prime; checking $n = 2, 4, 6$ gives primes $5, 17, 41$, and $n = 8$ gives $77 = 7\cdot 11$.

**Answer: 8**

prompt: The Purple Comet! Math Meet runs from April 27 through May 3, so the sum of the calendar dates for these seven days is $27 + 28 + 29 + 30 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 120$. What is the largest sum of the calendar dates for seven consecutive Fridays occurring at any time in any year?

solutions.title: Split across a month end
solutions.body:
Seven consecutive Fridays span $42$ days, so they cannot all be in one month. Within a month the Friday dates go up by $7$.

If the Fridays are in two months, the last Friday of the first month is at most $31$ and the first Friday of the next month is at most $7$. The largest possible dates are therefore $31, 24, 17, 10, 3$ in the first month and $7, 14, 21, 28$ in the second (a $35$th doesn't exist).

We need $7$ consecutive Fridays: $k$ at the end of the first month and $7 - k$ at the start of the next, with $7 - k\le4$. Best is $k = 3$: $31 + 24 + 17 + 7 + 14 + 21 + 28 = 142$. (With $k=4$: $82 + 42 = 124$; with $k = 5$: $85 + 21 = 106$.) Three months would mean two month ends inside the span, which only lowers the dates.

This happens, e.g., with Fridays on January 17, 24, 31 and February 7, 14, 21, 28 (as in 2003).

**Answer: 142**

solutions.title: Think of the wrap-around
solutions.body:
If no month ended, the dates would be $d, d+7, \dots, d+42$, but dates can't exceed $31$, so at some point we subtract the month length. Each Friday after the month change loses $30$ or $31$ compared with continuing. To keep the sum large we want the first month to have $31$ days and to end exactly on a Friday ($31$), so the next month starts its Fridays at $7$, the latest possible. Then the best split is three Fridays before ($17, 24, 31$) and four after ($7, 14, 21, 28$): sum $142$.

**Answer: 142**

prompt: John, Paul, George, and Ringo baked a circular pie. Each cut a piece that was a sector of the circle. John took one-third of the whole pie. Paul took one-fourth of the whole pie. George took one-fifth of the whole pie. Ringo took one-sixth of the whole pie. At the end the pie had one sector remaining. Find the measure in degrees of the angle formed by this remaining sector.

solutions.title: Add the angles
solutions.body:
The sectors are $120°, 90°, 72°, 60°$, totalling $342°$. Remaining: $360° - 342° = 18°$.

**Answer: 18**

prompt: A train car held $6000$ pounds of mud which was $88$ percent water. Then the train car sat in the sun, and some of the water evaporated so that now the mud is only $82$ percent water. How many pounds does the mud weigh now?

solutions.title: The dry part doesn't change
solutions.body:
The non-water part is $12\%$ of $6000 = 720$ pounds. Now it is $18\%$ of the mud, so the mud weighs $720/0.18 = 4000$ pounds.

**Answer: 4000**

solutions.title: Ratio
solutions.body:
The solids went from $12\%$ to $18\%$ of the total, i.e. the fraction grew by a factor $\frac{18}{12} = \frac32$. Since the solids stayed the same, the total shrank by $\frac23$: $6000\cdot\frac23 = 4000$.

**Answer: 4000**

prompt: How many distinct four letter arrangements can be formed by rearranging the letters found in the word **FLUFFY**? For example, FLYF and ULFY are two possible arrangements.

solutions.title: Count by the number of F's
solutions.body:
The letters are F, F, F, L, U, Y.

- One F: the other three letters must be L, U, Y: $4! = 24$ arrangements.
- Two F's: choose $2$ of L, U, Y ($3$ ways) and arrange $\frac{4!}{2!} = 12$: $36$.
- Three F's: choose $1$ of L, U, Y ($3$ ways) and place it ($4$ positions): $12$.
- No F's is impossible (only three other letters).

Total $24 + 36 + 12 = 72$.

**Answer: 72**

solutions.title: Place the non-F letters
solutions.body:
Choose which positions hold letters from L, U, Y and fill them with distinct letters; the rest are F (at most $3$ F's, so at least one non-F). With $j$ non-F positions: $\binom4j\cdot\frac{3!}{(3-j)!}$. $j=1$: $4\cdot3 = 12$; $j=2$: $6\cdot6 = 36$; $j=3$: $4\cdot6 = 24$. Total $72$.

**Answer: 72**

prompt: Find the number of non-congruent scalene triangles whose sides all have integral length, and the longest side has length $11$.

One plant is now $44$ centimeters tall and will grow at a rate of $3$ centimeters every $2$ years. A second plant is now $80$ centimeters tall and will grow at a rate of $5$ centimeters every $6$ years. In how many years will the plants be the same height?

solutions.title: Close the gap
solutions.body:
The first plant grows $\frac32$ cm per year, the second $\frac56$ cm per year. The first gains $\frac32 - \frac56 = \frac23$ cm per year on the gap of $80 - 44 = 36$ cm. Time $= 36\div\frac23 = 54$ years.

**Answer: 54**

prompt: The diagram shows a $20$ by $20$ square $ABCD$. The points $E$, $F$, and $G$ are equally spaced on side $BC$. The points $H$, $I$, $J$, and $K$ on side $DA$ are placed so that the triangles $BKE$, $EJF$, $FIG$, and $GHC$ are isosceles. Points $L$ and $M$ are midpoints of the sides $AB$ and $CD$, respectively. Find the total area of the shaded regions.

solutions.title: Top half and bottom half
solutions.body:
The four triangles each have base $5$ on $BC$ and height $20$ (apex on $DA$), area $50$ each.

Above $LM$ the shaded parts are the tips of the triangles: each tip is a similar triangle with half the height, so area $\frac14\cdot50 = 12.5$; four tips give $50$.

Below $LM$ the shaded parts are the regions outside the triangles. The bottom half has area $200$; the triangles occupy $4(50 - 12.5) = 150$ of it, leaving $50$.

Total shaded $= 50 + 50 = 100$.

**Answer: 100**

solutions.title: Compare matching horizontal lines
solutions.body:
At height $y$ above $BC$, each triangle is $5\left(1 - \frac y{20}\right)$ wide, so together the four triangles cover a width of $20 - y$ of the square's width $20$.

- At height $10 + t$ (above $LM$) the shaded width is the covered width: $10 - t$.
- At height $10 - t$ (below $LM$) the shaded width is the uncovered width: $20 - (10 + t) = 10 - t$.

Every line above $LM$ has a matching line below with the same shaded length, so the two shaded parts have equal area. Above $LM$ the shaded part is four tips of area $12.5$ each, i.e. $50$. Total $2\cdot50 = 100$.

**Answer: 100**

prompt: Aisha went shopping. At the first store she spent $40$ percent of her money plus four dollars. At the second store she spent $50$ percent of her remaining money plus $5$ dollars. At the third store she spent $60$ percent of her remaining money plus six dollars. When Aisha was done shopping at the three stores, she had two dollars left. How many dollars did she have with her when she started shopping?

solutions.title: Work backwards
solutions.body:
After store 3 she had $2$. Before store 3 she had $x$ with $0.4x - 6 = 2$, so $x = 20$.

Before store 2: $0.5y - 5 = 20$, $y = 50$. Before store 1: $0.6z - 4 = 50$, $z = 90$.

**Answer: 90**

solutions.title: Check forward
solutions.body:
Start with $90$: spend $36 + 4 = 40$, left $50$; spend $25 + 5 = 30$, left $20$; spend $12 + 6 = 18$, left $2$ ✓.

**Answer: 90**

prompt: In isosceles triangle $ABC$ sides $AB$ and $BC$ have length $125$ while side $AC$ has length $150$. Point $D$ is the midpoint of side $AC$. $E$ is on side $BC$ so that $BC$ and $DE$ are perpendicular. Similarly, $F$ is on side $AB$ so that $AB$ and $DF$ are perpendicular. Find the area of triangle $DEF$.

solutions.title: Coordinates
solutions.body:
$BD\perp AC$ and $BD = \sqrt{125^2 - 75^2} = 100$. Put $D = (0,0)$, $A = (-75, 0)$, $C = (75, 0)$, $B = (0, 100)$.

In right triangle $BDC$, the foot $E$ of the altitude from $D$ satisfies $BE = \frac{BD^2}{BC} = \frac{10000}{125} = 80$. Moving $80$ from $B$ toward $C$ (direction $(\frac35, -\frac45)$): $E = (48, 36)$. By symmetry $F = (-48, 36)$.

Area of $DEF = \frac12\cdot96\cdot36 = 1728$.

**Answer: 1728**

solutions.title: Similar triangles
solutions.body:
$DE = \frac{BD\cdot DC}{BC} = \frac{100\cdot75}{125} = 60$, and $DE$ makes the same angle with $BD$ as $BC$ makes with $DC$… simpler: $E$ is $36$ above $AC$ because $DE\cdot\sin\angle EDC = 60\cdot\frac{BD}{BC}\cdot$… In the right triangle $DEC$, $EC = \frac{DC^2}{BC} = 45$, so $E$ is $\frac{45}{125}\cdot100 = 36$ above $AC$ and $\frac{80}{125}\cdot75 = 48$ from $BD$. Then $EF = 96$ is horizontal at height $36$ and the area is $\frac12\cdot96\cdot36 = 1728$.

**Answer: 1728**

prompt: How many subsets of the set $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 12\}$ contain exactly one or two prime numbers.

solutions.title: Primes and non-primes separately
solutions.body:
The primes are $2, 3, 5, 7, 11$ (five of them); the other $7$ numbers can be chosen freely: $2^7 = 128$ ways.

Exactly one prime: $5$ ways; exactly two: $\binom52 = 10$ ways. Total $(5 + 10)\cdot128 = 1920$.

**Answer: 1920**

prompt: Rectangle $ABCD$ measures $70$ by $40$. Eighteen points (including $A$ and $C$) are marked on the diagonal $AC$ dividing the diagonal into $17$ congruent pieces. Twenty-two points (including $A$ and $B$) are marked on the side $AB$ dividing the side into $21$ congruent pieces. Seventeen non-overlapping triangles are constructed as shown. Each triangle has two vertices that are two of these adjacent marked points on the side of the rectangle, and one vertex that is one of the marked points along the diagonal of the rectangle. Only the left $17$ of the $21$ congruent pieces along the side of the rectangle are used as bases of these triangles. Find the sum of the areas of these $17$ triangles.

solutions.title: Bases times heights
solutions.body:
Each triangle has base $\frac{70}{21} = \frac{10}{3}$ on $AB$. The apexes are the $17$ marked points on $AC$ other than $A$, whose heights above $AB$ are $\frac{40k}{17}$ for $k = 1, \dots, 17$.

Sum of areas $= \frac12\cdot\frac{10}3\cdot\frac{40}{17}(1 + 2 + \cdots + 17) = \frac12\cdot\frac{10}{3}\cdot\frac{40}{17}\cdot153 = \frac12\cdot\frac{10}3\cdot360 = 600$.

**Answer: 600**

solutions.title: Average height
solutions.body:
The $17$ apex heights average to the height of the middle one, $\frac{40\cdot9}{17}$. Total area $= \frac12\cdot(\text{total base})\cdot(\text{average height}) = \frac12\cdot\left(17\cdot\frac{10}{3}\right)\cdot\frac{360}{17} = 600$.

**Answer: 600**

prompt: We have twenty-seven $1$ by $1$ cubes. Each face of every cube is marked with a natural number so that two opposite faces (top and bottom, front and back, left and right) are always marked with an even number and an odd number where the even number is twice that of the odd number. The twenty-seven cubes are put together to form one $3$ by $3$ cube as shown. When two cubes are placed face-to-face, adjoining faces are always marked with an odd number and an even number where the even number is one greater than the odd number. Find the sum of all of the numbers on all of the faces of all the $1$ by $1$ cubes.

solutions.title: Follow each row of three cubes
solutions.body:
Every face lies on exactly one straight line of three cubes running through the big cube (left–right, front–back or top–bottom), and each such line has exactly one visible end face (on the top, the left front or the right front). Along a line there are $6$ faces, and the rules fix each number from the previous one:

- within a cube (opposite faces): odd $o$ ↔ even $2o$;
- across a contact: odd $o$ ↔ even $o+1$.

Starting from a visible odd number $v$, the six faces are $v,\ 2v,\ 2v-1,\ 4v-2,\ 4v-3,\ 8v-6$, with sum $21v - 12$: so $1\to9$, $3\to51$, $5\to93$, $7\to135$, $9\to177$.

Starting from a visible even number: $2\to 2,1,2,1,2,1$ (sum $9$); $18 \to 18,9,10,5,6,3$ (sum $51$); $34\to 34,17,18,9,10,5$ (sum $93$).

Visible faces:

- Top: $2, 9, 3, 1, 7, 1, 5, 18, 1$ → $9 + 177 + 51 + 9 + 135 + 9 + 93 + 51 + 9 = 543$.
- Left front: $18, 1, 7, 2, 3, 34, 2, 5, 1$ → $51 + 9 + 135 + 9 + 51 + 93 + 9 + 93 + 9 = 459$.
- Right front: $1, 2, 1, 5, 1, 3, 1, 2, 9$ → $9+9+9+93+9+51+9+9+177 = 375$.

Total $543 + 459 + 375 = 1377$.

**Answer: 1377**

solutions.title: Group the visible numbers
solutions.body:
A visible $1$ gives the line $1,2,1,2,1,2$ and a visible $2$ gives $2,1,2,1,2,1$ — both sum to $9$. A visible $3$ and a visible $18$ give the same six numbers in opposite order ($3,6,5,10,9,18$), sum $51$; likewise $5$ and $34$ ($5,10,9,18,17,34$), sum $93$. A $7$ gives $7,14,13,26,25,50$ ($135$) and a $9$ gives $9,18,17,34,33,66$ ($177$).

The $27$ visible faces show: $1$ nine times and $2$ five times ($14$ lines of sum $9$), $3$ three times and $18$ twice ($5$ lines of $51$), $5$ three times and $34$ once ($4$ lines of $93$), $7$ twice and $9$ twice.

Total $= 14\cdot9 + 5\cdot51 + 4\cdot93 + 2\cdot135 + 2\cdot177 = 126 + 255 + 372 + 270 + 354 = 1377$.

**Answer: 1377**
